pending_commit.commit_message: Kerberos: Handle bad configuration Handle bad Kerberos configurations. Right now, the daemon crashes since the error happens during context initialization, but printing the error DCHECKs on the context. This CL fixes that and reports a proper error code. The UI should show error 19 (or a proper error saying that the config is bad) and the daemon should not crash. kerberos: Implement option to use login password Adds a use_login_password flag to AcquireTgt. If set, the login password is read from the kernel keyring and used as Kerberos password. In connection with the KerberosAccounts policy and the ${PASSWORD} placeholder this allows admins to prepopulate Kerberos tickets that log in automatically, so users get seamless, transparent Kerberos SSO. BUG=chromium:952240 TEST=Enabled KerberosEnabled policy, set policy "KerberosAccounts": [{ "principal":"test@chromeadm-lab.com", "password":"${PASSWORD}", }] change Gaia password to match test@chromeadm-lab.com password (see go/cros-ad-test-env), log in on Chrome OS with that Gaia account, verify in chrome:settings/kerberosAccounts that there is a valid ticket for this account. smbprovider: Save and restore password to the daemon-store. The password file is stored in the user's daemon-store directory, which is part of the user's cryptohome and encrypted at rest, and only accessible by the smbproviderd user. Because Mount() requests come from the logged-in profile, it is safe to assume the daemon-store directory exists. If the user explicitly removes the share, the password file should be deleted. BACKPORT: selinux: Permit bounded transitions under NO_NEW_PRIVS or NOSUID. Kernel v3.14 will need to backport this change first before backporting commit af63f4193f9f ("selinux: Generalize support for NNP/nosuid SELinux domain transitions") Upstream message: If the callee SID is bounded by the caller SID, then allowing the transition to occur poses no risk of privilege escalation and we can therefore safely allow the transition to occur. Add this exemption for both the case where a transition was explicitly requested by the application and the case where an automatic transition is defined in policy. Signed-off-by: Stephen Smalley <sds@tycho.nsa.gov> Reviewed-by: Andy Lutomirski <luto@amacapital.net> Signed-off-by: Paul Moore <pmoore@redhat.com> (cherry picked from commit 7b0d0b40cd78cadb525df760ee4cac151533c2b5) Signed-off-by: Qijiang Fan <fqj@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:963730 TEST=domain transition occurred for nnp processes (with Idaa729940d342f559fdeeb713bf808b07cc9c4cd) Change-Id: I708dc56ccc1d586e5ccacc8b6ddf83ecd198f50d Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1627072 Tested-by: Qijiang Fan <fqj@google.com> Commit-Ready: Qijiang Fan <fqj@google.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Jorge Lucangeli Obes <jorgelo@chromium.org>

Remove @allow_multiple_section_input decorator Certain RPC methods in FAFT were decorated with a custom property, @allow_multiple_section_input, which allowed multiple parameters to be bundled as a tuple. This change removes that custom solution. FAFT tests will now need to call the RPC multiple times in order to achieve the same effect. This change is particularly motivated by the upcoming protobuf, part of go/faft-grpc, which will define the parameters for all RPCs. It will be much clearer to read (section) than (section1, optional tuple_of_sections).
